title: Introduce multi-window epochal eval coordinator
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a coordinator that runs multiple evaluation windows in parallel and surfaces epochal regressions with configurable grace windows; no breaking changes to public APIs; opt-in via config.
description: Motivation: Current CI evals treat a single sliding window which can make transient regressions or bursty noise trigger unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces a multi-window epochal eval coordinator that runs multiple overlapping evaluation windows (short, medium, long) in parallel and aggregates signals with a configurable epoch and grace policy to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Summary of changes: add coordinator orchestration layer, new multi-window aggregator algorithm, per-prompt epochal state store, a lightweight decision rule DSL for progressive gating, a CI hook that emits structured `epochal_signal` events, and tests + docs. Design notes: windows run concurrently and report weighted signals; short window has high sensitivity but low persistence, long window has low sensitivity but high persistence; coordinator exposes thresholds, decay, and quarantine timers via config; a grace window parameter defers automatic fail actions until a minimum epoch count is observed. Migration: existing single-window jobs remain unchanged until projects opt-in by setting `EVAL_COORDINATOR_MODE=multi-window` or adding the new `coordination` block to eval.yml. Backwards compatibility preserved for existing CI hooks. Testing: unit tests for aggregation math, integration test that runs seeded synthetic regressions across windows, end-to-end smoke in CI. Checklist: - implement aggregator and coordinator code; - add unit/integration tests; - add CI hook and event schema; - update docs and quickstart; - verify perf and tune default thresholds. Related: ENG-1287 (reduce false-positive rollbacks), ENG-1320 (epochal alerting UX).
